content: Tomorrow's work do today, today's work now. If the moment is lost, when will you make amends?
author: Kabir
sourceWork: The Dohas of Kabir (Kaal Kare So Aaj Kar)
explanation:
In his most famous doha, the weaver-saint of Varanasi attacks the seductive illusion of 'someday.' We constantly postpone our moral duties, our creative work, and our heartfelt reconciliations, assuming that an endless supply of tomorrows is guaranteed to us. Yet breath is fragile, and circumstances shift in an instant. The only currency you possess is this unrepeatable present moment.

Act now with clarity and courage; tomorrow is a promissory note that may never be cashed.
practicalInsight: Take the task you have been repeatedly putting off until 'tomorrow' and complete at least the first crucial step within the next twenty minutes.
reflectionPrompt: What important conversation or creative endeavor are you risking by assuming you have unlimited time?
